claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi forms a dual-phase microstructure containing FCC solid solution and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The FCC phase in FeCoNiTi has intrinsically limited orbital moments.
The FeCoNiTi system exhibits multiple ferromagnetic transitions.
The C14 phase acts as a magnetic sink that suppresses the saturation magnetization associated with the FCC phase.
The C14 phase is Ti-rich, whereas the FCC phase is Fe/Co/Ni-rich.
Antiferromagnetic exchange occurs between Ti states in the C14 phase and Fe/Co/Ni moments in the adjacent FCC phase.
Ti atoms in the C14 Laves phase possess a magnetic moment.
Antiferromagnetic Ti–transition-metal coupling partially cancels the ferromagnetic alignment and reduces net saturation magnetization.
Electronic hybridization across FCC/C14 interfaces mediates the proposed antiferromagnetic exchange.
FCC/C14 phase boundaries pin magnetic domain walls.
Structural mismatch and distinct C14 magnetic anisotropy create local energy barriers for domain-wall motion in the FCC matrix.
Interfacial pinning and anisotropy raise the coercivity of dual-phase FeCoNiTi to approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase alloy has lower saturation magnetization than the theoretical maximum of pure FCC FeCoNi.
Single-phase FCC Fe-Co-Ni alloys have a coercivity cap of approximately 100 Oe because their orbital moments are insufficient and they lack strong pinning centers.
At 400 K, the C14 phase remains magnetically ordered or sufficiently coupled while the FCC phase remains ferromagnetic.
Decomposition of the C14 phase or loss of its magnetic coupling at 400 K would eliminate the proposed coercivity-enhancement mechanism.
A high-C14-fraction FeCoNiTi alloy and a negligible-C14, FCC control alloy should be compared by magnetic hysteresis measurements at 400 K.
Spin-polarized DFT should compare the FCC density of states at the Fermi level with and without an explicit C14 interface.
The hypothesis is falsified if the high-C14 alloy has coercivity below 200 Oe at 400 K or if DFT finds no significant interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling or Fermi-level spin-density modification.
